rounds.text: Mayur Leather Products Ltd is currently undergoing a significant fundamental turnaround, evidenced by a dramatic acceleration in profit growth to 75% over the trailing twelve months [E17]. This momentum is not a fluke, as the company has consistently improved its compounded profit growth from 5% over ten years to 30% over the last three years [E14, E16]. Consequently, the market is beginning to recognize this shift, with the share price reflecting this performance through an 83% compounded growth rate over the last three years and 103% over the past year [E20, E21]. The intrinsic value, calculated via discounted cash flow, sits at Rs 37 per share, providing an 18.3% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 30.4 [E38, E39]. While the company faces challenges, the recent earnings profile is robust, with net profit up 45% year-over-year and earnings growth actively accelerating [E50, E53]. Conceded: the company faces high valuation multiples [E1, E6, E11], a decline in promoter holding [E35, E48], and negative operating cash flow for the most recent period [E28, E29].

Mayur Leather Products Ltd currently trades at an extreme valuation, with a P/E ratio of 210x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 33.15x, significantly outpacing the sector benchmark of 13.6x [E11]. This premium is difficult to justify given the company's poor historical capital efficiency, evidenced by a median return on equity of -27% over the last decade [E22] and a current ROCE of only 0.81% compared to the sector benchmark of 10.66% [E10]. The financial position is further strained by a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.28x, indicating that debt exceeds net worth [E31], while operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -0.57 Cr in March 2026 [E29]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated recent profit growth [E17, E50] and a discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 37 per share [E38]. Despite these recent gains, the stock's price-led growth has significantly outpaced fundamental delivery [E41, E42], leaving the valuation vulnerable to any reversal in cyclical performance [E43].

The bear’s focus on the 210x P/E [E1] ignores that the company is in the midst of a powerful earnings turnaround, with profit growth accelerating to 75% over the trailing twelve months [E17] and 30% over the last three years [E16]. While the bear highlights historical capital efficiency [E22], it overlooks the current reality where the company has achieved a 20.3% ROE [E13] and a 20% median ROE over the last year [E25]. Conceded: the company faces leverage risk with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.28x [E31] and negative operating cash flow for the most recent period [E29]. However, this is offset by the fact that the company generated Rs 0.84 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E30], proving it can fund operations despite the reported cash flow metrics. Furthermore, the bear’s reliance on stale long-term averages ignores the current momentum, as the stock is currently trading below its intrinsic value of Rs 37 per share [E38]. Finally, the market is clearly recognizing this shift, as evidenced by the 103% share price growth over the last year [E21], which reflects the market's anticipation of the company's accelerating earnings profile [E53].

The bull’s reliance on recent profit growth [E17] ignores that the stock is trading at an extreme P/E of 210x [E1], a valuation that is fundamentally disconnected from the company’s long-term history of poor capital efficiency, including a 10-year median ROE of -27% [E22]. While the bull cites a 20.3% ROE [E13], this figure is contradicted by the broader data showing a current ROE of only 1.92% [E9] and a 3-year median ROE of 0% [E24]. Conceded: the company generated Rs 0.84 Cr in free cash flow [E30]. However, this does not negate the underlying structural weakness evidenced by negative operating cash flow [E29] and a cash conversion ratio of -0.50x [E28]. The bull’s optimism regarding the stock price [E21] fails to account for the fact that promoter holdings have plummeted by 37.52 percentage points since 2023 [E35], a significant red flag for long-term stability [E45, E48]. Finally, the company remains burdened by a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.28x [E31], which, combined with a P/B ratio of 4.86x [E2], suggests the market is pricing in perfection that the company’s inconsistent operating margins [E26] and low ROCE [E10] simply do not support.
